Apex Industrial Machinery Corp. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Industrial Machinery Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Industrial Machinery Corp.'s results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer; and Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Apex Industrial Machinery Corp.'s performance for the third quarter. We've made significant progress on several fronts, and I'd like to highlight a few key achievements. We delivered total revenue of $2.85 billion, up 18.8% year-over-year, exceeding our expectations through broad-based strength across segments. We achieved notable market share gains in key markets, expanding globally by 150 basis points to 4.2%, driven by automation and reshoring trends. Our book-to-bill ratio strengthened to 1.28x, signaling robust demand visibility with backlog hitting record levels. Operating margins expanded across segments, reaching 14.8% group-wide on favorable mix and cost discipline. Inventory levels are well-managed at $1.28 billion, with improved turns supporting efficiency. Backlog stands at $2.85 billion, up 28% year-over-year, providing clear conversion timelines. We've advanced our share repurchase program, executing $682 million year-to-date. Finally, strategic M&A activity, including key bolt-ons, bolsters our tech leadership and geographic reach.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Rivera to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Rivera (CFO):
Thank you, Johnathan. Turning to our financial performance, Apex Industrial Machinery Corp. reported $2.85 billion in revenue for the third quarter, representing an 18.8% increase year-over-year from $2.40 billion in Q3 2023. This marks our eighth straight quarter of double-digit growth, putting us 11% ahead of our internal guidance midpoint. Gross margin expanded to 48%, driven by a favorable shift toward high-margin automation solutions, pricing realization of 5-7% across the book of business, and supply chain normalization that compressed lead times for components like semiconductors and rare earths. Operating expenses were $950 million, reflecting disciplined investments in ECOP, our Enterprise Cost Optimization Program, resulting in operating income of $550 million. Our net income for the quarter was $420 million, or $1.70 per diluted share.

As we unpack the top-line momentum, growth was broad-based across our segments and regions. Core machinery sales, at 62% of revenue or $1.77 billion, surged 25% year-over-year, led by demand for our TitanFlex Series modular AI-optimized CNC mills that integrate with Siemens or Fanuc controls. Average selling prices rose 8% amid steel passthroughs, while units grew 15%, with electric arc furnace equipment up 35% on decarbonization plays akin to Nucor's expansions. Aftermarket parts and services contributed $795 million, or 28% of total, growing 12% organically as utilization on our 450,000-machine installed base held at 82%, bolstered by ForgeWatch IoT predictive maintenance subscriptions that jumped 40%. Systems integration and projects rounded out at $285 million, up 9%, including a $150 million battery gigafactory line contract similar to Panasonic's Nevada builds.

Geographically, North America drove 52% of revenue at $1.48 billion, up 22%, fueled by CHIPS Act semis capex and IIJA infrastructure, where we're displacing players like Caterpillar in off-highway gear. EMEA added $684 million, or 24%, rising 14% despite energy pressures, thanks to servo presses from our Frankfurt ramp. APAC hit $570 million, up 16%, with India and Southeast Asia exploding 45% on EV supply chains via Foxconn partnerships, offsetting China's softer 8%. Rest of world was flat at 4%. This reflects tailwinds like reshoring, with $250 million FY24 capex in Ohio and Texas forging to cut Asian reliance by 30%, tech differentiation in electrification like TitanEV forklifts with 40% lower TCO, and firm pricing against Chinese OEMs. We now guide FY24 revenue to $11.4-$11.7 billion, or 17-20% growth, with Q4 at $2.95-$3.05 billion.

Diving deeper into market share dynamics, which continue driving our outperformance, we track this meticulously via Gardner Intelligence and Statista against our $250 billion TAM in CNC machine tools, industrial robotics, and material handling. Globally, share expanded 150 basis points year-over-year to 4.2%, our third straight quarter of gains, powered by 12% revenue growth in automation and electrification, offsetting legacy hydraulic softness. In North America, our top market at 45% of sales, we grabbed 220 basis points to 14.3%, tied to reshoring with U.S. capex up 8% per ISM. PrecisionFlex CNC lathes with AI predictive maintenance cutting downtime 25% via IoT and ML displaced Haas in Ford and Boeing supplier deals, swelling backlog 18% to $2.1 billion at $450,000 ASPs despite steel inflation. ElectroForge battery stamping gained 3% in EV gear, partnering GM and Rivian.

Europe, 30% of revenues, added 80 basis points to 7.5% amid energy woes and 5% German orders drop per VDW, but EuroPress presses with 40% lower energy via servo drives boosted 1.8% in renewables, edging Trumpf at Vestas and Siemens Gamesa. We lost 50 basis points in metalforming to Italian discounters but countered with 15% Milan production ramp for 8-week leads and 92% OEE, eyeing 2% hydrogen share by FY25 on Green Deal funds. Asia-Pacific, 22% of sales, held flat at 3.8% overall; China lost 120 basis points to 2.9% on localization like Shenyang, with 7% volume drop and 4% ASP decline to $380,000. Yet QuantumLink cobots with 99.9% MTBF gained 4% in electronics via $200 million Foxconn iPhone deal. India/SE Asia surged 350 basis points to 6.2% on PLI schemes, Tata EV orders, and ForkLiftPro AGVs, with $50 million Bangalore plant targeting 10% share by 2026 at 15% TAM CAGR. Latin America gained 90 basis points to 4.1% on DrillMax rigs for Petrobras.

Our Tech-First pivot, with 20% R&D hike to 7% of sales yielding 15 SKUs like TwinCut simulators boosting throughput 18%, plus 60% Korean laser stake against Bystronic, underpins this. At 65% margins on automation versus 52% industry, we lead in reshoring and automation behind Fanuc/ABB. We guide another 100-150 bps Q4 gain for 4.3% full-year, fueling 10-12% FY24 organic growth over industry's 5%.

Turning to book-to-bill trends, a key leading indicator, we posted 1.28x this quarter, up from 1.15x Q2 and 1.02x Q3 2023—strongest since pre-2022 disruptions. Trailing 12-month is 1.18x, building $2.8 billion backlog, up 22% YoY or 9 months' billings. Automation/robotics led at 1.45x on RoboFlex 5000 AI vision arms up 35% for Tesla/Foxconn EV fabs. Precision CNC at 1.22x rode reshoring, with 5-axis mills up 28% for Boeing titanium work. Material handling/welding at 1.12x tracked energy recovery like Lincoln Electric. North America (52% bookings) hit 1.35x on CHIPS/IRA; APAC 1.42x on Taiwan semis; EMEA lagged at 0.98x on auto destocking; ROW 1.05x. $450 million FY24 capex, including Spartanburg CNC plant for 40% capacity and IndusCloud digital twins cutting leads to 10 weeks, supports this. We see 1.20-1.30x through year-end, with 4-6% pricing and VAVE for margins, derisking 75% FY25 revenue.

On operating margin performance by segment, group margins rose 210 basis points to 14.8%, via ECOP's lean sigma and AI analytics targeting 300 bps uplift by FY25. Heavy Machinery (38%, $1.2 billion up 5%) hit 12.2%, +150 bps, on 4.2% pricing and 7% Monterrey COGS cuts; NA strong at 15% on IIJA, EMEA 9.8%. Electrification like EHD-400 dozer eyes 14%. Automation & Robotics (28%, $875 million up 18%) soared 420 bps to 22.4% on cobot mix (IRB-500 up 35% at 28% margins), Shanghai scale dropping costs 12%, Digital Twin cutting NRE 25%; APAC 60% growth. Precision Components (22%, $700 million up 8%) steady at 13.5% (+90 bps) despite metal spikes, with GE turbine wins and ECOP overhead cuts; NA 16%, APAC 11%. Aftermarket (12%, $385 million up 12%) at 28.7% (+310 bps) on 42% attach via APM IoT for 15% uptime. Pricing/mix/volume/costs netted gains, guiding FY24 to 15.5-16%.

Backlog reached record $2.85 billion, up 28% YoY and 12% sequentially, with 1.35:1 book-to-bill above peers. Automation/robotics 42% ($1.2 billion) on data center AGVs; heavy machinery 31% ($885 million) on IIJA mining; fluid handling 18% ($513 million) on LNG/CCUS; energy tech 9% ($257 million). NA 52% ($1.48 billion) on CHIPS/EV; EMEA 26% ($742 million) on REPowerEU wind; APAC 17% ($485 million) on India infra; LatAm 5%. Conversion: 38% next 12 months ($1.08 billion), 68% in 24 ($1.94 billion), rest longer-lead. Digital twins accelerated throughput 15%, OTD to 94%; nearshoring cut leads 40%, headcount up 12%.

Inventory at $1.28 billion, +12% YoY but -8% sequentially from $1.39 billion peak, at 72 DIO versus 85 industry, turns 5.1x. Raw 42%, WIP 28%, FG 30%. Auto down 15% YoY on destocking; aerospace up 5% on Boeing ramps; energy steady. NA leanest $620 million (65 DIO); EMEA $380 million up 10%; APAC $280 million with higher safety. Precision Lean framework: AI forecasting (Blue Yonder, 12% MAPE) deferred $120 million; VMI 65% spend (Timken/Parker); MEIO for 98% service at 10-12% sales. Safety tuned 2.5 weeks, digital twins cut cycles 22%. Caps working capital at 4.2x versus peers.

On share repurchases, our $1.5 billion February authorization (post-$800 million prior) saw $682 million executed year-to-date (12.4 million shares at $55.02 avg), 4.8% of shares, via 10b5-1 plans. Q3 $285 million accelerated on $420 million FCF from 22% aftermarket growth at 52% margins. NA drove via IIJA; EMEA wind backlog; APAC shifted to India. ROIC 14.2% >9% WACC justifies over M&A/dividends, $0.48 EPS accretion to $11.40-$11.70 FY24 guide. $818 million remains, $400-500 million Q4 on $1.6-$1.7 billion FCF.

M&A added $1.2 billion deals: $650 million EuroBotix cobots for EMEA/tech synergies ($35 million), 25% cobot share; $350 million TaiMech actuators for semis de-risk; $200 million foundry divest for proceeds. Pipeline for battery/digital twins at 8-10x multiples, 12-15% organic +5-7% inorganic growth.

We remain committed to disciplined capital allocation and maximizing shareholder value.

Now, I will hand over to Lisa Chen, COO, for an operational update.

Lisa Chen (COO):
Thank you, Michael. Operationally, we've been focused on optimizing our manufacturing processes, improving supply chain efficiency, and enhancing our customer service capabilities. Leveraging digital technologies like digital twins and AI analytics, we've driven operational excellence, achieving 94% on-time delivery and 92% OEE in key plants. Our Precision Lean initiatives and nearshoring have reduced lead times significantly, while VMI with partners ensures resilience. We're also prioritizing employee health and safety, with skilled trades investments amid talent constraints.

And I will turn the call over to our CTO, Dr. Elena Vasquez, for an update on our technology roadmap.

Dr. Elena Vasquez (CTO):
Thank you, Lisa. We are committed to driving innovation and developing cutting-edge solutions for our customers. We are investing in research and development in areas such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, robotics, and the Internet of Things—7% of sales this year. Solutions for predictive maintenance, operational optimization, and enhanced performance include PrecisionFlex with 25% downtime cuts and ElectroForge for EV stamping. Our new ElectroForge battery stamping lines are significantly impacting the market, gaining 3% share in a 22% CAGR submarket through IRA-driven partnerships with GM and Rivian, accelerating adoption in gigafactories.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Lee (Morgan Stanley):
Good morning. Can you discuss the long-term impact of the new ElectroForge on your revenue and profitability?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, David. ElectroForge is transformative, addressing the exploding EV equipment TAM at 22% CAGR through 2028. By integrating AI-driven stamping with 40% energy efficiency, it's not only capturing 3% share early but projecting $500 million in annual revenue by FY26, with 65% gross margins versus 52% industry. Long-term, it enhances recurring aftermarket via IoT, boosting attach rates to 42% and overall profitability by 200 basis points through mix shift, while cross-selling into existing CNC customers amplifies network effects.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter (Goldman Sachs):
What are your expectations for revenue growth in the coming year?

Michael Rivera:
Emily, we're guiding FY25 revenue growth of 17-20%, building on FY24's $11.4-11.7 billion midpoint. This assumes 10-12% organic from backlog conversion and share gains, plus 5-7% inorganic from M&A pipeline. Tailwinds include semis/reshoring via CHIPS, EV infra, and 1.20-1.30x book-to-bill sustaining $3 billion backlog. Pricing holds 4-6%, aftermarket 12%+ growth. Risks like rates or tariffs are mitigated by 65% services/automation mix and FCF for flexibility.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Robert Kim (JPMorgan):
Can you discuss your plans for expanding your global footprint?

Johnathan Hale:
Absolutely, Robert. Global expansion targets 10% share in high-growth niches by 2026. APAC focus: $50 million Bangalore plant localizing 70% for India PLI EV/auto wins, countering China localization losses. EMEA: Milan ramp and EuroBotix integration for Green Deal hydrogen/wind. NA nearshoring via Monterrey/Spartanburg boosts reshoring. LatAm mining via DrillMax. Overall, balanced 52/26/17/5 split, leveraging M&A like TaiMech for semis resilience.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Anna Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Anna Patel (Barclays):
How are you managing rising energy costs?

Lisa Chen:
Great question, Anna. Energy costs are up 18% intra-quarter, but we've offset via EuroPress servo drives cutting consumption 40%, targeting sustainability. Localized production in Milan/Monterrey reduces logistics emissions/fuel. Digital twins optimize OEE to 92%, predictive maintenance cuts idles 30%. ECOP shaved overheads 5-10%, with hedging 60% exposure. Electrification roadmap like EHD-400 dozers promises 20% OPEX savings, positioning us ahead in renewables where peers lag.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes today's question-and-answer session.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you for your questions and your interest in Apex Industrial Machinery Corp. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
